# Late-Round Flyers for 1 to 3 USD

**Summary.** Spend at least three of your last four roster spots on 1 to 3 USD flyers who already start or are in a live role battle. The best of them are Kevin Porter Jr., Jakob Poeltl, Egor Dëmin, Derik Queen and Quentin Grimes, plus one cheap starting center. At the draft, write down the minutes each flyer needs. Cut him in the first two weeks if he misses that line. Pure injury handcuffs and players outside the 144-player pool go on the waiver watch list, not on our roster.

## What makes a real flyer

A flyer needs a real path to a role. Ask one question: does he start, or could he start soon? If reports say he will not start, pass. A name or a draft-day buzz is not a role. ([10-02](https://youtu.be/ZYllcj4o6_A?t=500), [10-01](https://youtu.be/aLP080hxizA?t=1390), [09-24](https://youtu.be/_vbAP5y182A?t=2322))

The ceiling has to be well above the price. Late picks should have top 70 upside, or at least a chance to beat their draft spot by 40 to 50 places. In our league the last dollar players sit near the end of the 144-player pool. A player whose best case is finishing where he was drafted is filler. You can find filler on waivers in October. ([10-01](https://youtu.be/EGdhmUgPAWY?t=1129), [09-23](https://youtu.be/C4vlgpJ62NI?t=2511), [09-07](https://youtu.be/E-KmhvyZ2CU?t=2414), [09-17](https://youtu.be/DubdKKhMWHo?t=1410))

Budget rule for our 12-player rosters: use at least three of your last four spots on upside flyers. Keep enough money to fill those spots at 1 to 3 USD each. Price decides whether a flyer makes sense. Cedric Coward and Collin Murray-Boyles have upside, but expert bids put them above the flyer range. Reed Sheppard works at 1 to 3 USD, but the experts fade ESPN's much higher rank on him. ([09-23](https://youtu.be/C4vlgpJ62NI?t=2511), [10-01](https://youtu.be/aLP080hxizA?t=1729), [Cedric Coward](../profiles/players/cedric-coward.md), [Collin Murray-Boyles](../profiles/players/collin-murray-boyles.md), [Reed Sheppard](../profiles/players/reed-sheppard.md))

## The best fits for our last spots

Kevin Porter Jr. has the clearest ceiling. The notes give him top 50 upside at about 29 minutes. Drop him if he plays under about 25. Jakob Poeltl is a starting center with top 70 upside if he holds about 28 minutes. Egor Dëmin projects with upside near 80th if he starts and his FG% climbs. ([Kevin Porter Jr.](../profiles/players/kevin-porter.md), [Jakob Poeltl](../profiles/players/jakob-poeltl.md), [Egor Dëmin](../profiles/players/egor-demin.md), [10-01](https://youtu.be/EGdhmUgPAWY?t=1129))

Derik Queen pays off if he wins the start from Yves Missi or Zion Williamson misses time. Quentin Grimes should start at about 30 minutes. His top 70 to 80 run needs Doncic or Reaves to miss time. On his own, his best case is about top 110. ([Derik Queen](../profiles/players/derik-queen.md), [Quentin Grimes](../profiles/players/quentin-grimes.md))

The next group of guards has a role but a lower ceiling. Jalen Green needs to keep the point guard job at 30-plus minutes. Reed Sheppard needs about 25 minutes, and you should drop him if he settles around 18. Darryn Peterson has top 15 upside long term, but the experts see no path to top 100 this season. Fred VanVleet is mainly a punt FG% guard with a weak playoff schedule. ([Jalen Green](../profiles/players/jalen-green.md), [Reed Sheppard](../profiles/players/reed-sheppard.md), [Darryn Peterson](../profiles/players/darryn-peterson.md), [Fred VanVleet](../profiles/players/fred-vanvleet.md))

## Cheap starting centers

A starting center with a decent profile is worth a late pick even if the job may not last. He gives you FG%, rebounds and blocks. The candidates here are Nic Claxton, Yves Missi, Isaiah Jackson, Moussa Diabaté, Daniel Gafford and Khaman Maluach. Each one has a clear job battle you can track. ([10-04](https://youtu.be/tnzmsYUA4yQ?t=804), [10-04](https://youtu.be/n4KkK-OJjqA?t=1139), [Nic Claxton](../profiles/players/nic-claxton.md), [Yves Missi](../profiles/players/yves-missi.md), [Isaiah Jackson](../profiles/players/isaiah-jackson.md), [Moussa Diabaté](../profiles/players/moussa-diabate.md), [Daniel Gafford](../profiles/players/daniel-gafford.md), [Khaman Maluach](../profiles/players/khaman-maluach.md))

Minutes decide whether a big is useful. One note says a late big needs about 30 minutes and is useless if he is split down to around 22. The player profiles use softer lines: about 25 minutes for Missi, Jackson and Diabaté, and about 24 for Maluach. Use 25 as the keep line. If a center sits near 22 after two weeks, drop him even if he starts. For guards and wings, about 27 minutes off the bench is enough. ([06-30](https://youtu.be/4GDfg2n2l8o?t=1075), [07-02](https://youtu.be/P6TNP-g0wzY?t=1334), [Yves Missi](../profiles/players/yves-missi.md), [Isaiah Jackson](../profiles/players/isaiah-jackson.md), [Moussa Diabaté](../profiles/players/moussa-diabate.md), [Khaman Maluach](../profiles/players/khaman-maluach.md))

## Where the experts disagree: injury handcuffs

One expert says a backup who is one injury away from starting is a valid late flyer. Others say waiting for someone else to get hurt is not enough, and a player who only pays off after an injury is a poor late pick. Our rule: draft a handcuff only if he also has his own path to minutes. Nikola Vučević qualifies as a swing if he gets 23 to 25 minutes behind Carter. Tari Eason and Paul Reed depend almost fully on injuries or rest plans for Durant and Duren. Leave them for the last dollar or skip them. Jalen Smith and Daniss Jenkins are already marked as quick waiver adds after an injury, not draft picks. ([10-02](https://youtu.be/ZYllcj4o6_A?t=2512), [10-01](https://youtu.be/aLP080hxizA?t=1390), [09-24](https://youtu.be/_vbAP5y182A?t=2338), [Nikola Vučević](../profiles/players/nikola-vucevic.md), [Tari Eason](../profiles/players/tari-eason.md), [Paul Reed](../profiles/players/paul-reed.md), [Jalen Smith](../profiles/players/jalen-smith.md), [Daniss Jenkins](../profiles/players/daniss-jenkins.md))

## Hedge pairs and stashes

Take two flyers in the same situation so at least one is likely to hit. In a starting-job battle, draft both, see who wins, and cut the other. Pairs in this pool: Yaxel Lendeborg with Gui Santos, Yves Missi with Derik Queen, Daniel Gafford with Morez Johnson Jr., and Quentin Grimes with Jake LaRavia. Jeremiah Fears pairs with Dejounte Murray as his handcuff. ([09-07](https://youtu.be/E-KmhvyZ2CU?t=1934), [09-10](https://youtu.be/dlo7L8Ru91A?t=1799), [08-24](https://youtu.be/g31YlwRe0XQ?t=2388), [Yaxel Lendeborg](../profiles/players/yaxel-lendeborg.md), [Gui Santos](../profiles/players/gui-santos.md), [Yves Missi](../profiles/players/yves-missi.md), [Derik Queen](../profiles/players/derik-queen.md), [Daniel Gafford](../profiles/players/daniel-gafford.md), [Morez Johnson Jr.](../profiles/players/morez-johnson.md), [Quentin Grimes](../profiles/players/quentin-grimes.md), [Jake LaRavia](../profiles/players/jake-laravia.md), [Jeremiah Fears](../profiles/players/jeremiah-fears.md))

We have four IL slots. Yanic Konan Niederhäuser can sit in one of them as a 1 USD final pick. He has late-season upside if he returns around Christmas and takes the job from Isaiah Jackson. Jackson's likely drop point is that same return. Do not chase Konan Niederhäuser to the 3 USD he got in a mock. ([Yanic Konan Niederhäuser](../profiles/players/yanic-konan-niederhauser.md), [Isaiah Jackson](../profiles/players/isaiah-jackson.md))

## When to cut and what it costs

At the draft, write down what has to happen for each flyer to pay off. Then check his minutes and starting role in the first two weeks. Late flyers are often drops. You take them to find out what their role is, then cut the ones that miss. With daily FAB and up to 6 adds a week, cutting a failed flyer costs very little. ([08-23](https://youtu.be/hm5-fiCa5S4?t=2248), [09-26](https://youtu.be/3UGI05PDvrE?t=1431), [09-24](https://youtu.be/_vbAP5y182A?t=2517), [08-26](https://youtu.be/sTtFUy7IoJI?t=423))

Expect most flyers to miss. Second-year players with an ADP of 101 to 150 reached the top 100 only 13% of the time. Undrafted sophomores almost never mattered. Even so, lean toward second-year players over third-year players, and keep uncertain rookies around picks 120 to 130. A failed late pick does not ruin a draft when the upside was real. ([09-04](https://youtu.be/gerS7ibpaJo?t=479), [09-04](https://youtu.be/gerS7ibpaJo?t=423), [09-07](https://youtu.be/gJUBAJaHzlU?t=481), [06-25](https://youtu.be/lOshTzDA4SA?t=867), [10-04](https://youtu.be/tnzmsYUA4yQ?t=1499), [10-04](https://youtu.be/n4KkK-OJjqA?t=1698))

Use the playoff schedule (weeks 19 to 21, ending 2027-03-28) only as a tie-breaker. Houston, Miami and Portland have only 10 games in those weeks. The Lakers go 3-4-3. Phoenix and Memphis go 4-4-4, and the Clippers go 4-3-4. Most flyers will be gone or traded long before March, so this matters only for the ones that hit. ([Reed Sheppard](../profiles/players/reed-sheppard.md), [Fred VanVleet](../profiles/players/fred-vanvleet.md), [Tari Eason](../profiles/players/tari-eason.md), [Pelle Larsson](../profiles/players/pelle-larsson.md), [Scoot Henderson](../profiles/players/scoot-henderson.md), [Jake LaRavia](../profiles/players/jake-laravia.md), [Jalen Green](../profiles/players/jalen-green.md), [Khaman Maluach](../profiles/players/khaman-maluach.md), [Cedric Coward](../profiles/players/cedric-coward.md), [Yanic Konan Niederhäuser](../profiles/players/yanic-konan-niederhauser.md))
